what: The one-second teaser, weighed against the 2.5-second one and against looping the full clip. Cut with UgcTranscoder::teaserCommand's own argv; only -t changed.

h264_same_source_only_-t_changed.note: The shop's real codec. Source: 8s 1080x1920 H.264 at 4000k, 4,053,294 B. Cut with -vf scale=360:640 crop -b:v 400k -c:v libx264 -preset veryfast -profile:v baseline -movflags +faststart -an.
h264_same_source_only_-t_changed.why_better_than_linear: A teaser is one keyframe plus cheap inter frames. The keyframe is paid once either way, so the 1.5s that comes off is the cheap part of the file.

vp9_the_measured_rail.note: What tools/ug3-preview.sh actually serves. VP9/WebM because Playwright's Chromium has no H.264. Source: 8s 1080x1920 testsrc2 at 4000k.

bytes_fetched_per_tile_over_real_http.note: From measurements-after.json, tools/m1-router.php serving real HTTP 206. Tile 1 and tile 2 point at the SAME content and differ in one thing: tile 1 has a teaser file.
bytes_fetched_per_tile_over_real_http.difference: 60.1x, for the same one second of picture

loop_length_measured_in_chromium.note: currentTime sampled every 100ms for 5s; a lap is the value a sample wrapped FROM. The 100ms sampling UNDERSTATES the true lap, so the before numbers are a floor.

cut_clip_native_loop.note: tile 1 has a teaser file and uses v.loop=true, so it never seeks at all
